1226	`installPath` when there is no link, and otherwise itself an `installPath` of this
1227	layout), and `contentSha256` is the raw SHA-256 of that package's manifest file
1228	bytes, retained in the closure.
1229	
1230	These rows are **not** snapshot inventory rows and must not be: the one shared
1231	discovery rule prunes `node_modules` by path segment, so the layout is a retained
1232	resolution observation of bytes the analysis read, joined by digest rather than by
1233	snapshot membership. `nodeModulesInReadSet` is exactly
1234	`nodeModulesLayoutDigest is not null`, the layout is a **required** binding input
1235	whenever it is non-null, and a retained layout that no context selected is refused
1236	rather than drifting into the resolution. With the layout present, bare specifiers
1237	resolve normally; with it absent, `nodeModulesInReadSet=false` and every bare
1238	specifier is an `unresolved-module-specifier` edge with scope `external` — never an
1239	implicit install. Both branches are now constructible; before this record existed
1240	only the second one was.
1241	
1242	`SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` (deterministic function of the unit listing and
1243	`package.json`; version 1 pinned): `allowJs=true`, `checkJs=false`,
1244	`module=node16`, `moduleResolution=node16`, `target=es2022`, `jsx=preserve` iff any
1245	`.jsx/.tsx` root exists else absent, `strict=false`, `skipLibCheck=true`,
1246	`types=[]`, `noEmit=true`, roots = every `.ts/.tsx/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` file under
1247	the unit excluding `node_modules`, `.git` and host ignore conventions. No option is
1248	read from the environment. A synthesizer change is a universe change.

1250	### 2.3 `NativeContextV2` (Rust)
1251	
1252	**There is exactly one native-context record and one `H` domain per language.**
1253	`NativeContextV2` is the **Rust** context; `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (§2.4) is the
1254	TypeScript one. Neither is a general "native context": a universe binds the record of its
1255	own language and refuses the other.
1256	
1257	Descriptor (domain `native.context.rust.v2`): `{schemaVersion:2, targetTriple,
1258	hostTriple, toolchain: ToolchainIdentityV1, toolClosure: ToolClosureV1, baseCfg,
1259	resolverVersion, dependencySourceSetId, unifiedFeaturesId, preparedOutputSetId|null,
1260	configProjection: CargoConfigProjectionV2}`.
1261	
1262	`rustcDevLlvmDigest` is at **`NativeContextV2.toolchain.rustcDevLlvmDigest`**, inside
1263	`ToolchainIdentityV1` — not a top-level field of the context (a citation that says only "in
1264	native-context schema 2" is reachable but under-specified). Its value is the 64-hex suffix
1265	of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=rust-dev-llvm` closure, so `"closure2:" +`
1266	the field must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it;
1267	`admit_native_context('rust', …)` performs exactly that join against the retained closure
1268	descriptor and tree.
1269	
1270	`ToolClosureV1` = `{rustc, cargo, linker|null, ar|null, procMacroServer, closureId}`

1272	signed `closure2` named by `closureId`. **Every tool that runs is in this
1273	closure**: `rustc`, `cargo`, the linker rustc spawns when a build script or
1274	proc-macro crate is linked, `ar`, and the proc-macro server. No `PATH` lookup, no
1275	system `cc`, no `RUSTC`/`CARGO`/`RUSTUP_*`/`CARGO_HOME` from the environment. If a

1277	`UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` there (`native.execution-not-authorized`, cause
1278	`linker-unavailable`); it never falls back to a system linker.

1280	The host resolved-inputs adapter computes the context before PlanId; the worker
1281	recomputes it after sealed inputs are received and refuses with
1282	`Unavailable(native-context-mismatch)` before Analyze if any byte differs (§9.5).

1284	### 2.4 `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (TypeScript/JavaScript)
1285	
1286	Descriptor (domain `native.context.typescript.v2`): `{schemaVersion:2, languageMode,
1287	toolchain: TypeScriptToolchainIdentityV1, toolClosure: TypeScriptToolClosureV1,
1288	configProjection: TypeScriptConfigProjectionV2, moduleResolutionMode, packageModuleType,
1289	nodeModulesLayoutDigest|null, lockfileIdentity|null}`.

1291	`TypeScriptToolchainIdentityV1` = `{compilerName:"typescript", compilerVersion,
1292	compilerPackageDigest, typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot, standardLibraryComponentDigests[],
1293	libSelection[]}`. `TypeScriptToolClosureV1` = `{compiler, runtime, closureId}`.
1294	
1295	**Exact field locations and producing recipe.** Every value is computed by the host
1296	resolved-inputs adapter before PlanId from **admitted, retained** bytes; none is read from a
1297	worker claim, a `tsc --version` string or the environment.
1298	
1299	| Field | Produced from |
1300	|---|---|
1301	| `toolchain.compilerVersion` | the `semanticVersion` of the **admitted signed compiler closure manifest** named by `toolClosure.closureId`; admission refuses when the two differ, so a version string and the bytes it labels cannot drift apart |
1302	| `toolchain.compilerPackageDigest` | a member digest of that retained `kind=toolchain` closure tree |
1303	| `toolchain.typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` | identity §3's existing recipe: the **64-hex suffix** of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=stdlib` closure. `"closure2:" +` the value must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it |
1304	| `toolchain.standardLibraryComponentDigests` | the **complete** declaration-file inventory of that retained stdlib tree — one row per `.d.ts` member, selected or not, `component` = the member basename, sorted by `component`. A tree in which two paths share a basename refuses `native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<name>` rather than resolving the join arbitrarily |
1305	| `toolchain.libSelection` | the effective `lib` **names** the resolved `compilerOptions` select after `target` defaulting, sorted; each must map to a retained component under the published name-to-component join below. These are `lib` names (`es2022`), never declaration-file names |
1306	| `toolClosure.compiler`, `toolClosure.runtime` | raw digests of the bundled compiler and of the bundled JavaScript runtime that executes it, both members of the signed closure named by `closureId`. No `PATH` lookup, no system `node`, no `NODE_OPTIONS`/`NODE_PATH`/`TS_NODE_*` from the environment |
1307	| `configProjection.honoredOptions` | the closed subset of the **effective** resolved `compilerOptions` (or of `SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` under `js-synthesized`) that changes program membership, module resolution or checking |
1308	| `configProjection.strippedOptions` | every option removed, with a typed reason (`selects-an-executable`, `emits-output`, `reads-the-environment`, `acquires-types-from-the-network`, `not-a-resolution-or-membership-option`). 1309	| `configProjection.configGraphPaths` | every `tsconfig`/`jsconfig` file of the resolved `extends` graph, in the snapshot, sorted by logical path; empty under `configOrigin=synthesized` |
1310	| `nodeModulesLayoutDigest` | raw SHA-256 of `C(ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1)` — the retained resolution read-set layout — or `null` exactly when `nodeModulesInReadSet=false` |
1311	| `lockfileIdentity` | `{kind, path, contentSha256}` of the admitted lockfile, or `null` when `lockfileKind=none` |
1312	
1313	**Retained trees.** The stdlib closure and the compiler closure are retained **whole** —
1314	complete foundation `closure` descriptor and complete file tree — and joined to the selected
1315	compiler. `admit_native_context` recomputes each closure identity from its retained record
1316	and refuses `native.native-context-closure-unretained`,
1317	`native.native-context-closure-identity-mismatch` or
1318	`native.native-context-closure-kind-mismatch` before any digest comparison. The stdlib merkle
1319	root is therefore never a bare number a caller can assert.
1320	
1321	**`libSelection` → `standardLibraryComponentDigests`: the published join.** The
1322	two arrays hold different vocabularies on purpose and neither is rewritten into
1323	the other. `libSelection` holds effective **`lib` names** — the values
1324	`configProjection.honoredOptions.lib` carries (`es2022`, `dom`), which is why the
1325	two are compared directly. `standardLibraryComponentDigests[].component` holds
1326	**declaration-file basenames** of the retained stdlib closure tree
1327	(`lib.es2022.d.ts`). Because the join between them is enforced at context
1328	admission with its own typed refusal, it is published here rather than left to
1329	ecosystem convention; two hosts inventing different mappings would admit and
1330	refuse the *same* retained context bytes differently, which is a public admission
1331	divergence, not implementation freedom.
1332	
1333	| Rule | Statement |
1334	|---|---|
1335	| Fold | `fold(n)` is Unicode **Default Case Conversion `toLowercase(X)`**: the **full**, **non-tailored**, **context-sensitive** default lowercase mapping (Unicode Standard §3.13 / UAX #21). It is the **same single fold** the honored-`lib` agreement below uses, and this section defines no other: no NFC/NFKC step, no trimming, no alias table, no prefix or suffix matching. Reference implementation `native_evidence_model.v2.lib_name_fold` |
1336	| Mapping | `component(n) = "lib." + fold(n) + ".d.ts"`. Total, deterministic and **one-directional**: a selected name maps to exactly one component basename, and a component is never mapped back into a selected name |
1337	| Membership | for every `n` in `libSelection`, `component(n)` must be an element of the declared `component` set. A name whose component is absent refuses `native.native-context-lib-not-retained:<n>` — §10 route `request-rejected` (2) / `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, before PlanId |
1338	| Equality | `{fold(n) : n ∈ libSelection}` must equal `{fold(m) : m ∈ honoredOptions.lib}`. `honoredOptions.lib` is required and non-empty in the closed resolved context, so this agreement always applies and is **not** weakened by the mapping. Two `libSelection` entries with the same fold refuse `native.native-context-field-mismatch:duplicate-lib-selection`; a set disagreement refuses `native.native-context-field-mismatch:libSelection` |
1339	| Order | `libSelection` is sorted by the raw UTF-8 bytes of the **retained, unfolded** names; `standardLibraryComponentDigests` by the raw UTF-8 bytes of `component`. Each record keeps its own specified order for hashing — folding is a comparison, never a rewrite of a retained value, and neither array is re-spelled into the other's vocabulary |
1340	
1341	**What `fold` is, and what it is not.** The three plausible operations are genuinely different
1342	and only one of them is the one this admission performs, so it is named rather than approximated.
1343	
1344	| Discriminator | `fold` (**full default lowercase**) | simple lowercase | case folding |
1345	|---|---|---|---|
1346	| `U+0130` LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT ABOVE | `U+0069 U+0307` — **two** code points, through `SpecialCasing.txt` | `U+0069`, one code point | `U+0069 U+0307` |
1347	| `U+039F U+03A3` (sigma in **final** position) | `U+03BF U+03C2` — the `Final_Sigma` condition | `U+03BF U+03C3` | `U+03BF U+03C3` |
1348	| `U+03A3 U+039F` (sigma **not** final) | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` |
1349	| `U+00DF` LATIN SMALL LETTER SHARP S | `U+00DF` — unchanged | `U+00DF` | `U+0073 U+0073` |
1350	
1351	So `fold` is **not** `Simple_Lowercase_Mapping` (it expands, and it is position-dependent) and
1352	**not** `Case_Folding` (sharp s is unchanged). It is **non-tailored** — the root locale, with no
1353	Turkish/Azeri dotless-i and no Lithuanian tailoring — so the result must never depend on an ambient
1354	locale, an environment variable or a host language setting.
1355	
1356	**Version custody, and the portability consequence it does not hide.** The result of a default case
1357	conversion is determined by the Unicode case data the host carries, so `fold` is deterministic
1358	**given a case-data version**, and this design binds the reference derivation to one:
1359	`native_evidence_model.v2.UNICODE_CASE_DATA_VERSION`, currently **UCD 15.0.0**, the version the
1360	table above was measured against. Two hosts on different case data can fold the same name
1361	differently — for a code point unassigned in one of them (an unassigned code point folds to itself),
1362	or for one whose mapping changed between the versions — and because `libSelection` enters the
1363	context descriptor and therefore `PlanId`, that would be an admission divergence, not a cosmetic
1364	one. This contract does **not** claim the fold is invariant across every runtime. It requires the
1365	version to be a declared, checkable property rather than whatever the runtime happens to ship:
1366	`unicode_case_data_agreement()` reports the running version against the declared one so drift is
1367	disclosed instead of silently changing an outcome. Nothing here narrows the field to ASCII to
1368	sidestep the question — it is simply true that every `lib` name in the pinned compiler's own option
1369	vocabulary is ASCII, where all three operations above coincide, and that is a fact about the current
1370	vocabulary rather than a constraint on the value.
1371	
1372	**Custody: the two arrays answer different questions.** `libSelection` is the
1373	*configuration-facing* record of what the resolved options selected, and it is
1374	what the universe/config agreement is checked against.
1375	`standardLibraryComponentDigests` is the *tree-facing* **complete** declaration
1376	inventory of the retained stdlib closure — one row per `.d.ts` member with its
1377	raw digest, selected or not. So the selection never narrows the inventory and the
1378	inventory never adds a selected name: a missing inventory row refuses
1379	`native.native-context-stdlib-inventory-incomplete:<basename>`, and a tree in
1380	which two paths share a basename refuses
1381	`native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<basename>` — the mapping's
1382	target would not be unique, and an arbitrary resolution is exactly what this
1383	refusal exists to prevent. The join reads **no other input**: not a
1384	caller-supplied map, not a filesystem lookup, not a compiler query, not the
1385	`typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` value on its own.
1386	
1387	**No platform *field*, and the identity is still platform-specific.** Unlike the Rust context there
1388	is no `targetTriple`/`hostTriple`, because TypeScript *resolution semantics* — which specifiers
1389	resolve, which subjects are examined, what is checked — are platform-invariant by design (§1.1).
1390	That is a design selection of this contract, not a measurement, and it is **not** a claim that the
1391	identity is platform-invariant: `toolClosure.closureId` names a signed closure whose foundation
1392	`closure` descriptor includes `platform`, so the same source analysed with the platform-specific
1393	executables of two families mints two `nativeContextId`s — as it must, because different bytes ran
1394	(`typescript-context-identity-is-platform-specific-through-its-signed-tool-closure`).

1395	
1396	**Universe and Plan binding.** `typescript-v2.nativeContextId` is
1397	`H("native.context.typescript.v2", descriptor)` in the `Sha256Text` form. `PlanId` binds the
1398	same digest through `plan.nativeContextDigests`, which takes the **bare 64 hex** (§11, the
1399	foundation `plan` record's spelling) and is a canonical **set**: several units of one language
1400	legitimately share one context, and identical admitted contexts collapse to one member — that is
1401	deduplication of an identical descriptor, never of two different ones.
1402	
1403	`bind_typescript_universe(universe, admission, context)` refuses a universe whose `nativeContextId`
1404	this host did not mint (`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch`) and refuses a Rust-minted context
1405	outright (`native.native-context-language-mismatch`). The **retained context bytes are a required
1406	argument**: there is no context-free admit path, because an optional field-agreement check is not a
1407	rule — a caller that omitted it would obtain exactly the bypass this join exists to close. Omission
1408	is the typed refusal `native.universe-context-not-supplied`
1409	(`typescript-universe-bound-without-the-retained-context-refuses`); context bytes that do not hash to
1410	the admitted id refuse
1411	`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch:context-bytes-are-not-the-admitted-ones`.
1412	
1413	Given those bytes the two records must **agree where they overlap**: a matching `nativeContextId`
1414	commits to the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them, so `languageMode`,
1415	`packageModuleType`, `allowJs`, `checkJs`, `lockfileKind`, `nodeModulesInReadSet`,
1416	`jsDiagnosticsEnabled`, `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `configOrigin`, the `extends`-graph emptiness and the
1417	synthesized-options presence are each checked against the context and refuse
1418	`native.universe-context-field-mismatch:<field>`.
1419	
1420	The context itself also has mandatory agreement rules. `moduleResolutionMode`
1421	equals `configProjection.honoredOptions.moduleResolution`. `libSelection` is
1422	strictly sorted by UTF-8 name bytes, contains no duplicate names under the
1423	published `fold`, and selects the same folded name set as the honored `lib` list
1424	— the same `fold` the component join above uses, and the only one this section
1425	defines; each record retains its specified order for hashing. The closed resolved context
1426	always materializes that nonempty list. When source configuration omits `lib`,
1427	the resolver supplies the pinned compiler's target-default library selection
1428	in both records; `null` is not an alternate resolved spelling.
1429	`standardLibraryComponentDigests`
1430	has strictly unique component keys in UTF-8 order. Context admission refuses any
1431	contradiction before its digest may enter Plan. In synthesized mode every value
1432	in `synthesizedOptions` equals the corresponding honored option, and an absent
1433	optional `jsx` means honored `jsx` is null. Presence alone is insufficient.
1434	These are semantic agreement checks in addition to closed schema validation;
1435	internal diagnostic suffixes remain operational refusal evidence, not new public
1436	DomainDetail codes.
1437	
1438	**Independent derivation (§9.5) applies to TypeScript exactly as to Rust.** The worker
1439	recomputes the context from its own sealed inputs; a differing byte is
1440	`Unavailable(native-context-mismatch)` before Analyze.

1466	## 3. Sealed dependency inputs (AR-07)
1467	
1468	### 3.1 `DependencySourceSetV1`
1469	
1470	Identity domain `native.dependency-source-set.v1`. Closed descriptor:
1471	`{schemaVersion:1, language:"rust", lockfileIdentity, packages:
1472	[DependencyPackageSourceV1…] sorted by (name, version, sourceId) UTF-8 bytes,
1473	completeness:{state, missing[]}}`.
1474	
1475	`DependencyPackageSourceV1`:
1476	
1477	| Field | Rule |
1478	|---|---|
1479	| `name`, `version` | exact `[[package]]` values from `Cargo.lock` |
1480	| `sourceKind` | `registry \| git \| path \| vendored` |
1481	| `sourceId` | exact `source` string from `Cargo.lock`, or `""` for path packages |
1482	| `lockChecksum` | 64-hex from the lock `checksum`, or `null` for git/path |
1483	| `fileManifestSha256` | H(`native.dependency-file-manifest.v1`, sorted `[{path, contentSha256, byteLength}]`) |
1484	| `fileCount`, `totalBytes` | exact uint64 |
1485	| `acquisition` | `{mode: in-snapshot-path \| in-snapshot-vendored \| imported-descriptor, descriptorId: ImportId\|null, vendorPath\|null}` |
1486	| `checksumVerification` | `tarball-matched \| self-consistent \| not-applicable \| mismatch` — `mismatch` refuses the whole set |
1487	| `provenanceAssurance` | `registry-authenticated \| declared` |
1488	
1489	Verification rules (feedback 3 corrected):
1490	
1491	- **DS-1 (registry, vendored tree)** A vendored directory carries a self-asserted
1492	  `.cargo-checksum.json`. Its `package` field equalling `lockChecksum` proves
1493	  nothing about the files: an attacker rewrites file contents and every `files`
1494	  entry while preserving `package`. The host therefore checks internal
1495	  consistency only (`package == lockChecksum`, every listed file's SHA-256
1496	  matches, no extra or missing files) and records `checksumVerification =
1497	  self-consistent`, `provenanceAssurance = declared`. Inconsistency is `mismatch`
1498	  and refuses the set. The reference model contains the mutation
1499	  (`ds1-mutation-preserving-package-checksum-stays-declared`): the mutated tree is
1500	  still admitted, and it is still *declared*, never authenticated.
1501	- **DS-2 (registry, tarball)** Only the exact `.crate` tarball whose SHA-256
1502	  equals `lockChecksum` yields `tarball-matched` / `registry-authenticated`. The
1503	  host extracts it deterministically into the CAS and computes the file manifest
1504	  itself. An extracted tree plus `.cargo-checksum.json` is DS-1.
1505	- **DS-3 (git)** The import supplies the checked-out tree for the exact `#rev`;
1506	  `not-applicable` / `declared`; the file manifest identity is the binding.
1507	- **DS-4 (path)** Path dependencies live in the snapshot; nothing is imported.
1508	- **DS-5 (no ambient reads)** `$CARGO_HOME/registry`, `~/.cargo`, `vendor/`
1509	  outside the snapshot, or any host path is read **only** as the explicit,
1510	  user-named source path of an import step (§7). Any acquisition mode outside the
1511	  closed set, or any fetch URL, refuses. No network fetch exists in any first-party
1512	  code path (design invariant, conformance-checked; not a confinement claim).
1513	- **DS-6 (completeness)** The set is complete for a target when every package
1514	  activated by `UnifiedFeaturesV1` is present with `checksumVerification ≠
1515	  mismatch`. An incomplete set is admitted with `completeness.incomplete` and
1516	  typed `input-closure-incomplete` Coverage for dependent crates; it never blocks
1517	  syntax analysis.
1518	
1519	`declared` provenance is disclosed wherever the package matters: in the Plan
1520	(through the set descriptor), in `AuthorizedExecutionV2.owners[].provenanceAssurance`,
1521	and in the pre-execution sentence (§5.2). Facts derived from declared sources are
1522	still Plan-bound Coverage inputs; the disclosure is what changes.
1523	
1524	### 3.2 Custody and transport
1525	
1526	The host stores admitted dependency sources in its content-addressed store keyed
1527	by `fileManifestSha256`; Plan-bound by `dependencySourceSetId`. Transport uses
1528	protocol-3 frames `DependencySourceManifest / DependencySourceChunk /
1529	DependencySourceSeal / DependencySourceAccepted` (§9.2) with the same byte-exact,
1530	digest-verified, reject-before-use discipline as the snapshot. The worker mounts
1531	the accepted files read-only at `.opensip/deps/v1/<name>-<version>/…` in its
1532	private scratch materialization. Nothing is fetched lazily.
1533	
1534	### 3.3 Cargo configuration: verified carrier, exact flags (feedback 5, 10)
1535	
1536	Primary source (`doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html`, read 2026-09-06):
1537	Cargo reads `.cargo/config.toml` (and legacy `.cargo/config`) from the current
1538	directory and **every ancestor**, plus `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, merging arrays;
1539	it also honors `CARGO_*` environment overrides and knobs that select executables
1540	(`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `target.*.linker`, `target.*.runner`),
1541	credentials and network. Stock Cargo has no switch that disables ancestor
1542	discovery, and this contract does not claim `--config` replaces the stack.
1543	
1544	The first-party `opensip-cargo-adapter` therefore establishes a **verified
1545	ancestor carrier** (`CargoConfigProjectionV2`, all checked by
1546	`cargo_config_admission` in the model):
1547	
1548	- **CC-1** Before every Cargo invocation, every ancestor directory of the private
1549	  scratch root is checked for `.cargo/config.toml` and `.cargo/config`. Presence
1550	  is a refusal (`native.ambient-cargo-config`, exit 4), never a merge and never a
1551	  silent skip. `ancestorCarrierVerified=true` is recorded in the context.

1553	  invocation; its `config.toml` is absent by construction.

1696	## 4. Resolution completeness (AR-12)
1697	
1698	### 4.1 Two different completeness claims
1699	
1700	A Coverage entry commits two things that were previously conflated:
1701	
1702	1. **Examined universe** — the exhaustive examined subject/target partition
1703	   (`subjectScopeCommitment`, retained). "Did we look at every subject?"
1704	2. **Resolution completeness** — whether every reference/import/call edge
1705	   originating in the examined subjects was resolved to a binding at the requested
1706	   rung, *after resolution was actually attempted over the whole partition*.
1707	   "Could we see every consumer?"
1708	
1709	### 4.1a Producing recipe for `subjectScopeCommitment` (closed)
1710	
1711	The retained C-2 selector deferred computation and verification. This is the successor
1712	recipe; nothing about the historical artifact changes.
1713	
1714	**Recipe.** `subjectScopeCommitment` is the foundation **subject-scope** identity of the
1715	examined partition, re-spelled in the native `Sha256Text` text form:
1716	
1717	```
1718	scope2      = identity-and-evidence H("subject-scope", D)          -> "scope2:"  + hex
1719	commitment  = "sha256:" + the same 64 hex                          -> Sha256Text
1720	```
1721	
1722	where `D` is the closed foundation record
1723	`identity-schemas.v3.json#/$defs/subject-scope`
1724	`{schemaVersion: 2, snapshotId, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse, relation, resolution,
1725	enumeratorClosure, subjects}`.
1726	
1727	**Inputs, exactly, and where each comes from.** `snapshotId` is the admitted `snapshot2`.
1728	`relation`/`resolution` are the Coverage key's own relation and rung. `sourceUniverse` and
1729	`targetUniverse` are the bare 64-hex universe digests of the same key (§2, §11).
1730	`enumeratorClosure` is the `closure2` of the Plan-bound enumerator that produced the
1731	partition. `subjects` is the **complete** examined subject inventory that enumerator
1732	enumerated over that snapshot, a canonical set (foundation ordering, duplicates refuse
1733	rather than dedupe). **Encoding**: the foundation canonical encoder and `H` frame, imported,
1734	not restated. There is **no native `H` domain for this field**: one preimage, one digest,
1735	two admitted textual spellings (§11).
1736	
1737	**Join with `scope2`.** The commitment is the *identical* digest to the `scope2` the host
1738	binds into the `coverage2` descriptor (`coverage.scopeId`). It is therefore not a second
1739	commitment and cannot drift from the scope it names. Its purpose is that the Coverage
1740	*payload* — the bytes whose `payloadDigest` mints `coverage2` — carries the provider's
1741	in-band commitment to the partition it claims to have examined, which the host then checks
1742	against a value the provider never supplied.
1743	
1744	**Where it is produced and checked (`admit_coverage_result_v3`, the admitted native producer

1745	boundary).** For every `CoverageResultV3` a provider sends, before any `coverage2` exists:
1746	
1747	1. The host builds `D` from **its own** enumeration and mints `scope2`. A provider-supplied
1748	   commitment is never an input to this step.
1749	2. `key.relation`, `key.resolution`, `key.sourceUniverse`, `key.targetUniverse` must equal
1750	   `D`'s (`native.coverage-key-scope-mismatch:<field>`).
1751	3. `key.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the computed commitment
1752	   (`native.subject-scope-commitment-mismatch`).
1753	4. `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the key's
1754	   (`native.examined-universe-commitment-mismatch`) and
1755	   `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectCount` must equal `len(D.subjects)`
1756	   (`native.examined-universe-subject-count-mismatch`). A provider that examined a narrower
1757	   partition than the host enumerated is detected here, and by nothing else.
1758	5. RC-2 (§4.3) is rechecked over the same partition.
1759	6. Only then is `coverage2` minted from `{schemaVersion: 2, scopeId, payloadSchemaDigest,
1760	   payloadDigest}`. `payloadSchemaDigest` is the raw SHA-256 of the **exact registered schema
1761	   DOCUMENT bytes** (§7.2). A caller may restate it but never choose it: a value that is not the
1762	   registered document's digest refuses `native.coverage-payload-schema-not-registered`
1763	   (`coverage-payload-schema-digest-a-caller-chose-is-refused`).
1764	
1765	Every refusal above is `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION` (`operational-failed` 4) under the §10
1766	fault law: a worker that lies about its partition contributes no facts, no Coverage and no
1767	Run. This is not a Coverage deficiency; an admitted-but-incomplete input is (§10).
1768	
1769	**Coverage use (`coverage_view_use`).** A `view2` may name a `coverage2` only if that
1770	`coverage2` was admitted at the boundary above and its `scope2` is one of the view's own
1771	`scopeIds`. A hash-valid `coverage2` whose subject scope sits outside the evaluated view is
1772	refused exactly as hidden finding evidence is (identity §3), rather than joined silently.
1773	
1774	**No circularity.** `D` names the snapshot, the universes and the enumerator closure. A
1775	universe descriptor (§2) names its native context, tools and config projection; a native
1776	context names closures; none of them names a scope, a Coverage, a view, an evidence record
1777	or a Run. The derivation order is therefore total and acyclic: closures → native context →
1778	universe → `scope2` → commitment → Coverage payload → `coverage2` → `view2`. The foundation
1779	scope *descriptor* whose raw digest is `scopeDigest` (§1.4, workspace roots and path
1780	prefixes) is a different record with a different job and is not this commitment.
1781	
1782	Cases: `subject-scope-commitment-is-the-scope2-identity-in-native-sha256-text-form`,
1783	`subject-scope-commitment-binds-the-snapshot-not-only-the-subject-list`,
1784	`coverage-admission-mints-coverage2-from-the-host-subject-scope`,
1785	`coverage-commitment-chosen-by-the-claimant-is-refused`,
1786	`coverage-producer-chosen-narrower-examined-partition-is-refused`,
1787	`coverage-examined-subject-count-that-disagrees-with-the-enumeration-is-refused`,
1788	`coverage-key-naming-a-universe-outside-the-host-scope-is-refused`,
1789	`coverage-complete-claimed-over-an-admitted-unresolved-edge-is-refused-at-the-boundary`,
1790	`coverage-incomplete-over-an-exhaustive-partition-admits-with-the-same-commitment`,
1791	`coverage-use-requires-the-subject-scope-to-be-in-the-evaluated-view`,
1792	`coverage2-whose-subject-scope-is-outside-the-view-is-refused`,
1793	`coverage2-never-admitted-at-the-producer-boundary-is-refused-in-a-view`,

1795	`coverage-payload-schema-digest-a-caller-chose-is-refused`. The two positive coverage cases

1834	### 4.3 View entry v3 and `CoverageResultV3`
1835	
1836	Per `(relation, rung, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse)` the view entry is
1837	`ViewEntryV3`:
1838	
1839	```
1840	{ "relation", "resolution": rung, "coverage": "complete"|"unknown",
1841	  "examinedUniverse": {"subjectScopeCommitment", "subjectCount"},
1842	  "resolutionCompleteness": {
1843	     "state": "complete"|"incomplete"|"partial"|"not-attempted"|"not-applicable",
1844	     "attempted": bool, "examinedExhaustive": bool,
1845	     "stageTerminal": "complete"|"unavailable"|"budget-exhausted"|"provider-fault"|"cancelled"|"crash"|null,
1846	     "unresolvedEdgeCount": uint64, "unresolvedEdgeClasses": sorted unique UnresolvedEdgeKindV1 },
1847	  "closedWorld": ClosedWorldV2 (§4.5),
1848	  "derivationKinds": sorted subset of {annotated, jsdoc-declared, compiler-inferred},
1849	  "confidenceMillionths": uint64, "deficiency": null|DeficiencyV2, "nativeCause": null|NativeCause }
1850	```
1851	
1852	`CoverageResultV3` on the wire = `{schemaVersion:3, key: CoverageKeyV2, entry}`;
1853	the host wraps it in `coverage2` by exact `payloadSchemaDigest`/`payloadDigest`.
1854	
1855	- **RC-1 (applicability, total over the registered pairs).** `state` is decided by
1856	  the **rung**, through membership in the closed five-member resolved set
1857	  (`resolved-target`, `resolved-binding`, `resolved-callee`, `checked`,
1858	  `from-resolved-calls`) — **never** by how many rungs the relation's ladder has.
1859	  Over the registered `(relation, rung)` pairs of the single ladder authority
1860	  `foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-relation-registry`:
1861	  - a **resolved** rung must never claim `not-applicable`; its state is one of
1862	    `complete`/`incomplete`/`partial`/`not-attempted` under RC-2. The five such
1863	    pairs are `imports@resolved-target`, `references@resolved-binding`,
1864	    `calls@resolved-callee`, `types@checked` and `reachability@from-resolved-calls`.
1865	  - **every other registered rung is `not-applicable`**, minted with
1866	    `attempted=false`, `unresolvedEdgeCount=0` and `unresolvedEdgeClasses=[]`.
1867	    Those are the remaining twelve pairs: the one-rung relations
1868	    `file@enumerated`, `package@manifest-declared`, `vcs-change@vcs-reported`,
1869	    `declares@syntactic`, `literal@syntactic`, `control-flow@syntactic`,
1870	    `clones@normalized-body-hash`; the weaker rungs of the multi-rung relations
1871	    `imports@syntactic-specifier`, `references@syntactic-name-match`,
1872	    `calls@syntactic-callee-name` and `types@annotated`; and
1873	    **`unresolved-edge@observed`** (§4.4).
1874	  - `unresolved-edge@observed` is stated explicitly because an entry is owed for
1875	    an ordinary Run — `resolutionCompleteness` is a **required** member of
1876	    `ViewEntryV3` and the matrix advertises the capability `SUPPORTED-DESIGN` in
1877	    five of six language modes — and because `observed` is **not** a resolved
1878	    rung: the relation records the edges resolution did *not* close, so it makes
1879	    no resolution claim of its own. Stated precisely, and no more strongly than
1880	    the evidence allows: RC-1 as previously written refused **neither** a
1881	    `complete` nor a `not-attempted` entry on this pair, so two conforming
1882	    implementations could commit **different** Coverage records — and therefore
1883	    different `coverage2` identities — for the same underlying Coverage question.
1884	    Those alternatives are *not* two spellings of one identical record: `complete`
1885	    and `not-attempted` necessarily differ in `attempted` as well as in `state`,
1886	    and the blind consumer-B v5 vector's two candidates also differed in other
1887	    committed fields. This is a determinacy gap in the contract, **not** a digest
1888	    collision and not a divergence over byte-identical observations.
1889	  - `reachability` is the case that shows why ladder length is not the rule: it is
1890	    a **one-rung** relation whose single rung `from-resolved-calls` **is**
1891	    resolved, so it is never `not-applicable`.
1892	  - a relation or a rung outside the closed registered vocabulary refuses on the
1893	    schema enum, and a rung belonging to **another** relation's ladder is never a
1894	    live value anywhere: `membershipRule` decides membership against *that*
1895	    relation's own `ladder`, and that pair check is applied to the subject scope
1896	    when it is minted, to the Coverage entry at the producer boundary and again at
1897	    retained closure (RC-0 below), to a fact at fact admission, and to a
1898	    Requirement or view use, which resolves no ladder index for it
1899	    (`required-relation-missing`). RC-1 assigns **no** state to an unrecognised
1900	    pair: `not-applicable` is a claim about a *registered* pair and is never a
1901	    fallback for one the registry does not know.
1902	
1903	  **RC-0 runs first and is relation-specific.** Before any state rule, the entry's
1904	  own `(relation, rung)` must be a **registered pair**: the rung must be a member
1905	  of *that relation's* `ladder`. The rung vocabulary is shared across relations, so
1906	  a schema-valid `resolution` proves nothing — `unresolved-edge@enumerated` names
1907	  two registered tokens and no registered pair, and it is refused. This check is
1908	  independent of any fact: a **fact-free** entry, over an empty or non-matching
1909	  examined scope, is judged the same way, because a fact-admission guard cannot

2066	Evaluated in this order; every applicable cause is collected and the most specific
2067	by §10 precedence is reported. `satisfied=true` may carry `disclosures`.

2151	### 4.8 Type derivation provenance (feedback 12)
2152	
2153	The v1 draft capped JSDoc-free JavaScript type facts at `confidenceMillionths ≤
2154	900000`. That number had no evidence rationale: a compiler-inferred type is exact
2155	under the admitted universe, and JSDoc presence is not a calibrated probability.
2156	Replacement: every `types@checked` fact carries `TypeDerivationV1` =
2157	`{derivationKind: annotated|jsdoc-declared|compiler-inferred, confidenceMillionths:
2158	1000000, confidenceMethod: "native.confidence.v1", checkJs, limitations}`.
2159	`native.confidence.v1` is the versioned, conformance-bound method
2160	"declared-exact: every admitted checked fact is 1000000 under its universe; no
2161	value below 1000000 is produced by a native provider". Rule authors express
2162	"declared types only" through `derivationPolicy=declared-only` (§4.2), which
2163	yields the typed `derivation-policy-unmet` deficiency, not a fake percentage.
2164	`checkJs` is recorded because it changes diagnostics, not derivation.
2165	
2166	**The two clauses have different scopes, and the second is deliberately the wider
2167	one.** The first names the method of `TypeDerivationV1`, whose
2168	`confidenceMillionths` is a schema **constant** `1000000` and whose
2169	`confidenceMethod` is the constant `native.confidence.v1`: that record exists only
2170	on a `types@checked` fact. The second — *no value below 1000000 is produced by a
2171	native provider* — is **not** narrowed to `types@checked`. It is a **provider
2172	emission law** over this whole bundle: no native provider of any relation emits a
2173	confidence below 1000000, because a native fact is exact under its admitted
2174	universe and this design publishes no calibrated probability for any relation. It
2175	is not read as types-scoped, and reading it that way would be a *weakening* — it
2176	would permit a native `clones` or `references` provider to emit a fabricated
2177	percentage, which is exactly what §4.8 removed.

2251	names here are `effects` field names; the pinned table is over seven closed
2252	permission **tokens**, and the correspondence was determinate by elimination but
2253	published nowhere, so an implementer had to infer it. It is stated:
2254	
2255	| `effects` field | Permission token | `ENFORCED` in v9 (child-process) | What the value means |
2256	|---|---|---|---|
2257	| `subprocess` | `PT-PROC-EXEC-DECLARED` | `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` | No mechanism prevents the effect; the record states what was asked and answered. |
2258	| `filesystemWrite` | `PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE` | `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` | Same. See the scope note below. |

2260	| `environment` | `PT-ENV-READ` | `ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION` | The child's environment is constructed by the host, so the capability is never conferred *in this execution mode*. |

2265	   processes, so the `child-process` column is the applicable one. In v9's
2266	   `in-host-process` mode *every* token including `PT-ENV-READ` is
2267	   `DISCLOSURE-ONLY`, because a component sharing the host's address space shares
2268	   its environment. Quoting `ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION` without its mode would
2269	   over-claim.

2271	   names the *host's own state store*. Neither it nor any grant over it confers

2273	   precisely that nothing prevents writes anywhere: the executing code holds the
2274	   invoking user's ambient authority throughout. `filesystemWrite` here is a

2301	### 5.3 What the preparation step does (feedback 4)
2302	
2303	Owned by the host resolved-inputs adapter (never the semantic worker), after
2304	snapshot seal and dependency-source admission, before PlanId:
2305	
2306	1. Verify the carrier (§3.3 CC-1..CC-5); materialize snapshot and dependency
2307	   sources read-only in private scratch; write the single projected
2308	   `.cargo/config.toml`; construct the environment.
2309	2. Check current trust and revocation state (security owner's clock), then for
2310	   each owner in order: re-check revocation (`before-each-owner`), run the bundled
2311	   Cargo to compile and execute the build script or to build the proc-macro crate
2312	   for the selected cfg set (`cargo check --offline --frozen --locked --target
2313	   <triple>` restricted to the owners; the linker used is the closure linker;
2314	   nothing is installed).
2315	3. **Inside this same authorized step**, drive the bundled compiler's expansion
2316	   through the closure proc-macro server for every invocation site in the
2317	   workspace and dependency crates that names one of the built proc-macro crates,
2318	   and capture the expanded token text per site as `macro-expansion` rows; capture
2319	   `cargo:` directive output as `build-script-directives` rows. Loading the
2320	   proc-macro dylib *is* executing repository code; it happens here, under the
2321	   principal, with the live boundaries, and nowhere else.
2322	4. **Capture required generated data, discard executable products** (R2). For
2323	   each build-script owner: capture the `cargo:` directive lines as a
2324	   `build-script-directives` row; capture as `generated-file` rows the regular
2325	   data files under `OUT_DIR` named by the crate's
2326	   `include!/include_str!/include_bytes!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), …))` sites when
2327	   those are statically determinable, else every regular data file under
2328	   `OUT_DIR` within the PO-4 bounds; discard the build-script binary, every
2329	   dylib/object/archive/executable product and unreferenced scratch files; discard
2330	   the proc-macro dylibs. Referenced paths the script did not produce are recorded
2331	   (`missingReferencedPaths`) and become typed unknowns at analysis. Nothing of
2332	   `OUT_DIR` survives except the captured data rows
2333	   (`preparation-capture-keeps-referenced-data-discards-executable-products`).
2334	   The result is `PreparedOutputSetV3` (`kind: authorized-execution`).
2335	
2336	The semantic worker then consumes the inert set through the protocol
2337	(`PreparedOutputManifest/Chunk/Seal`), looks up expansions by exact site key, and
2338	executes nothing. `RepositoryResolutionV3.workerExecutesRepositoryCode` is the
2339	constant `false`. An external preparer may supply the same inert shape
2340	(`kind: imported-descriptor`, `declared` provenance, §3.6 PO-3); it can never
2341	supply a dylib.

2343	### 5.4 Failure, retry, cancellation, recovery
2344	
2345	| Event | Outcome |
2346	|---|---|
2347	| Owner build script exits non-zero | row `failed`; other owners continue; owner analyzed non-prepared |
2348	| Revocation observed before an owner | step stops; no further owner runs; rows already captured are discarded; `request-rejected` (`native.execution-not-authorized`) |
2349	| Wall or byte bound exceeded | whole step `operational-failed` (4); no row admitted. Existing `HOST.IO_FAILURE` with detail `native.prepare-bound-exceeded`. Not `BudgetExhausted`: a preparation bound is a safety bound of the adapter |
2350	| Cancellation | kill the process group, discard partial OUT_DIR and captured rows, `interrupted` (130) |
2351	| Retry | idempotent by `(dependencySourceSetId, toolchainDigest, cfgSetId, owners manifest)`; an identical inert set already in custody is reused without re-execution and without re-prompt when a policy record covers it |
2352	| Host crash mid-step | scratch reclaimed by ordinary crash reconciliation; no partial set is visible to Plan construction |
2353	| Ambient Cargo config found | `operational-failed` (4), `native.ambient-cargo-config`; never merged |
2354	| Imported set replaces in-host preparation | allowed; PO-0/PO-1/PO-3 apply |

2381	
2382	`minOccurrences 2`; `minBodyBytes 64` (exact); `minTokens 20` (L1–L3,
2383	cross-tsjs); `minTokens 50` (near); `nearThreshold 800000` millionths;

2386	### 6.3 Bodies and language-specific exclusions
2387	
2388	Body spans are function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies.
2389	**Import exclusion means candidate exclusion, not byte editing** (R5): a span that
2390	consists solely of import/`use`/`extern crate`/top-level `require` declarations,
2391	module/file headers, shebangs, license headers, `#![...]` inner attributes or
2392	`declare`-only TypeScript declarations is an *import-only body* and is excluded
2393	as a clone candidate in every mode. A body that is kept is hashed over its
2394	**exact verbatim bytes**: an internal `use`, `import()`, `require` or directive
2395	inside a function body is part of the preimage and is never stripped, rewritten
2396	or normalized away at L0 (`clone-import-only-body-excluded-and-kept-bodies-hash-verbatim`:
2397	two bodies differing only by an internal `use` line are not exact clones).
2398	
2399	| Language | Kept significant at every level | L2 removes | L3 renames |
2400	|---|---|---|---|
2401	| TypeScript/JavaScript | string/template literal contents, regex literals, JSX text, `'use strict'`/`'use client'` directives, `/// <reference>` and `// @ts-*` directives, decorators | non-directive comments | local `let/const/var`, parameters, local function names, destructured locals; **not** properties, imports, exports, globals, `this` members |
2402	| Rust | macro invocation token trees verbatim, attributes including `#[cfg]`, string/byte/raw literals, lifetimes | non-doc comments | local `let` bindings, parameters, closure parameters, pattern bindings; **not** fields, paths, generics, trait names, macro-introduced names |
2403	
2404	Fact identity is same-language: `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` is
2405	in the preimage, so a TypeScript body never groups with a JavaScript or Rust body
2406	in `exact`/`normalized`/`structural`, even with identical bytes.
2407	
2408	### 6.4 TS/JS cross-language decision (feedback 9)
2409	
2410	Decision: `languageId` **stays** in exact fact identities (a `.ts` and a `.js`
2411	body are different facts). Cross-TS/JS matching is a separate **candidate-only**
2412	mode `cross-tsjs` under the named deterministic syntax projection
2413	`tsjs-erasure-v1`:
2414	
2415	- Removed before L3 normalization: type annotations, `type`/`interface`
2416	  declarations, type parameter lists, `as` assertions, `satisfies`, non-null `!`,
2417	  definite-assignment `!`, `declare`/`readonly`/`abstract`/access modifiers,
2418	  `implements` clauses, `import type`/`export type`.
2419	- **Never removed**: tokens that TypeScript compiles into runtime behavior —
2420	  `enum`/`const enum`, parameter properties (`constructor(private x)`),
2421	  value-bearing `namespace`, decorators, `import =`. A body containing any of them
2422	  is **excluded** from cross matching with reason
2423	  `runtime-significant-ts-tokens` and the token list; it is not projected.
2424	- Output rows carry `projectionId=tsjs-erasure-v1`, `authority=candidate-only`,
2425	  `semanticEquivalenceClaimed=false`, `automaticDeletionEligible=false` as schema
2426	  constants. A cross candidate is never a baseline member, never a Control input,
2427	  never a repair prerequisite. Execution-inputs `CloneCandidateGroupV2.members`

2433	  and cross-TS/JS remain candidate-only by this section; they mint no `fact2`

2896	A `null` deficiency requires a `null` cause: a cause without a deficiency names
2897	why nothing went wrong.
2898	
2899	**Some rows are scoped by relation, because their owning law is.** `§4.7` and
2900	`sufficiency_v2` apply `derivationPolicy` only where the relation is `types` and
2901	the requirement asks `declared-only`; no other relation has a derivation policy,
2902	so no other relation's entry can be short of one. Checking the `derivationKinds`
2903	carrier *alone* let a `references` entry that merely carried the same array value
2904	declare this deficiency, and a complete Run admitted it. The registry row now
2905	carries the owning `relations` list and admission refuses an entry outside it.
2906	
2907	This is **declaration support, not an obligation**, and the two must not be
2908	confused. Enforced: an entry that *declares* `derivation-policy-unmet` is for
2909	`types` and actually carries `compiler-inferred`. Not enforced, and deliberately
2910	so: whether a given requirement *demands* it. `compiler-inferred` types are exact
2911	under the admitted universe, carry no probabilistic confidence, and are entirely
2912	valid under `derivationPolicy=any`; they become a deficiency only under
2913	`declared-only`, which is `sufficiency_v2`'s question against a `RequirementV2`
2914	and is never derived from a Coverage entry. Both directions are held by controls.
2915	
2916	**Multiple simultaneous causes, and precedence.** An entry carries **one**
2917	deficiency and **every** carrier at the same time — but *what each carrier
2918	retains differs*, and an earlier revision of this paragraph generalised the
2919	strongest case to all of them by saying the scalar "loses nothing". Accurately,
2920	per carrier:
2921	
2922	- `resolutionCompleteness.unresolvedEdgeClasses` is a genuine **set** and retains
2923	  *every* applicable unresolved class at once, already forced by RC-2 to equal
2924	  the admitted `unresolved-edge` facts of the view. Here nothing is lost, and
2925	  this is why enum members would have been the wrong fix.
2926	- `closedWorld` and `derivationKinds` are independent fields that retain their
2927	  own state whatever the declared deficiency is.
2928	- `input-closure-incomplete`'s carrier is a **single scalar** `NativeCause`, and
2929	  a Run can genuinely be missing several inputs at once — two absent crates, or
2930	  an absent crate *and* an unavailable generated file. For that row the retained
2931	  cause is a **selected** one, not the full set.
2932	
2933	**The selected-scalar limitation, stated rather than engineered around.** The
2934	producer names the cause it acted on; Run closure checks that the named cause is
2935	lawful for the deficiency and cannot enumerate the inputs that were not named.
2936	What *is* fully retained beside it is the rest of the entry and the Run's own
2937	evidence — the missing dependency sources, prepared rows and generated files are
2938	retained records in their own right — so a consumer needing the complete set
2939	reads those, not the scalar. **No multi-cause format is introduced** merely to
2940	make this paragraph true: the bounded source and ownership laws are unchanged and
2941	the limitation is published so no consumer reads the scalar as exhaustive.
2942	
2943	Which single member is declared when several
2944	apply is the precedence order above, applied by the owning sufficiency
2945	evaluation against a **Requirement**. That selection is deliberately **not**
2946	re-derived from the entry alone, and the limit is stated rather than worked
2947	around: several conditions are requirement-relative (external-consumer state
2948	matters only for a universal negative about an exported target; the confidence
2949	floor lives in the Requirement), and **RC-3** makes `coverage: complete` with
2950	`state: incomplete` and *no* deficiency a valid honest entry. Forcing a
2951	deficiency out of exhibited entry evidence would refuse lawful Runs. What is
2952	decidable from the entry, and what is therefore enforced, is the other
2953	direction: a **declared** deficiency must be **supported** by the entry's own
2954	committed evidence.
2955	
2956	**Retained and public routes are different, and both are named.** *Retained*:
2957	the whole `ViewEntryV3` lives inside the `coverage2` record whose payload and
2958	schema digests the Run commits, so every carrier above is retained evidence a
2959	verifier re-derives. *Public*: the **deficiency** projects outward as its own

2961	and `derivation-policy-unmet` are already members — and the **cause** travels as
2962	typed detail in the `coverage2` record the host termination names by its
2963	`coverageId`, exactly as this section has always said for the
2964	`nativeCause`-carried rows. No new public code is added for this projection of a lawful entry's deficiency and cause. The refusal branches later in this section separately add four public detail codes; those additions do not change this projection.

3101	**A refused value can exceed the diagnostic bound, and the projection is
3102	bounded.** `DomainDetail.subject` is `BoundedText` (1024) while a *structurally
3103	valid* `languageMode` may be 4096 characters; the composed subject then reached
3104	4149 and made the whole failure envelope schema-invalid at
3105	`termination.domainDetail.subject` or `errors[0].subject`. `bounded_subject`
3106	elides: the registered **key** is preserved verbatim — it selects the code, the
3107	class and the origin — and only the offending value is elided, keeping a leading
3108	window plus the SHA-256 of the untruncated subject's UTF-8 bytes. Emitting the untruncated
3109	string would be schema-invalid, dropping the subject would lose attribution, and
3110	reclassifying the input error as success would be false. The code, class and
3111	origin are never changed by the elision.
3112	
3113	The encoding is normative, and its **units** are stated because they differ
3114	between the two operations. Let `raw` be the composed subject
3115	`<registered key>[:<value>]` as an **admitted Unicode scalar string**. Length and
3116	slicing count **Unicode code points**, which is what `BoundedText`'s JSON Schema
3117	`maxLength` counts — not UTF-8 bytes and not UTF-16 code units. If
3118	`len(raw) ≤ 1024` the subject **is** `raw`. Otherwise it is
3119	
3120	```
3121	raw[: 1024 − len("...#sha256:") − 64] + "...#sha256:" + hex(SHA256(raw.encode("utf-8")))
3122	```
3123	
3124	— the marker `...#sha256:` is ASCII, the digest is exactly 64 lowercase hex
3125	characters, the SHA-256 input is exactly `raw` encoded as UTF-8 with **no**
3126	additional normalization, and the result is exactly 1024 code points. A
3127	non-ASCII value therefore has a UTF-8 byte length that may exceed 1024 while its
3128	scalar length does not, and the two operations must not be conflated.
3129	
3130	Two distinct long values are distinguished under the **ordinary
3131	collision-resistance assumption** for SHA-256; this is not a claim that collision
3132	is impossible. **The guarantee is confined to what is published** — the bounded
3133	subject and its digest. This contract does **not** promise a separate retained
3134	store of the untruncated value and names none; a host that keeps its own
3135	operational log may match it by recomputing this digest, which is why the digest
3136	is published at all.

3401	More precisely, the **compilation target** decides, not the package. Cargo
3402	documents an `edition` on a target that **defaults to** `package.edition` when

3406	package edition* misses a supported override, and a universe whose package

3408	therefore **no single-edition fast path**: a `clones` fact over a Rust universe
3409	requires the committed ownership relation whatever the package map looks like,

3453	vocabulary `WorkspaceUnitV2` already uses, under the ordinary canonical
3454	repository-path admission with no added restriction. **`WorkspaceUnitV2` and
3455	`UnitMembershipV1` cannot supply this binding**, and that is a granularity

3457	(`cargo-package`, `cargo-workspace`), while one package holds several targets

3459	existing discovery vocabulary instead of competing with it.
3460	
3461	**Because the selection is committed inside the record whose `h-identity` the
3462	universe names, a different selection is a different record, a different identity
3463	and therefore a different `sourceUniverse`.** That is what makes the required case
3464	representable: one physical source path compiled by two targets at two editions is
3465	validly analysed **under each selection, one at a time**, each with its own
3466	correct dialect and its own body identity, and **no relation payload changed** to
3467	make it so.
3468	
3469	Selection is exact and total, and the order of decision is fixed so each step has
3470	its own cause. No committed ownership refuses. `enumeration: partial` refuses
3471	**before any row is read**. Rows are those whose `path` **equals** the enclosing
3472	fact's anchor path — never a prefix, never a nearest directory, never a first
3473	match — and no row at all refuses as not-compiled. Rows are then restricted to
3474	`selectedUnitIds`, and a path compiled only by **unselected** targets refuses as
3475	not-selected rather than borrowing an out-of-scope edition. Selected owners whose
3476	effective editions **agree** are admissible — the ordinary shared-file and
3477	lib-plus-test-target case. Selected owners that **disagree** are an ambiguous
3478	unselected request and refuse. §2.1's retained-input admission independently
3479	requires every marker and owned path to be a source of the same snapshot, every
3480	selection and ownership row to name a declared unit, and every deferring unit to
3481	name a crate the same `edition` map declares.
3482	
3483	**Selected scope is not incomplete enumeration.** A selection says these targets
3484	*are* the analysis, so an owner outside them is deliberately out of scope; it is
3485	committed in the identity, so every consumer sees it and it changes the universe.
3486	`partial` says the producer did not finish, so an owner *inside* the selected
3487	scope may exist that is not listed and could contradict a listed one — a gap in
3488	knowledge, invisible as a selection, admitting no dialect at all. Silently
3489	omitting a conflicting owner from the table is not a selection either: an
3490	omission leaves no trace, whereas a selection is part of the universe identity.
3491	Partial evidence stays useful under the existing law rather than voiding a Run —
3492	the clones scope mints no body identity, its Coverage carries the incompleteness,
3493	and the predicate and seal are indeterminate.
3494	
3495	The consequence is the one that matters: an **ordinary mixed-edition workspace
3496	has a representable valid form**. Each path is owned by units of one edition, so
3497	bodies of *both* editions are admissible in the *same* universe, each carrying
3498	its own dialect. Only a path genuinely compiled under two different editions
3499	refuses, which is a real ambiguity in the input rather than a gap in the law.

3673	canonical record-size and work budgets still apply; exceeding them is explicit
3674	incomplete analysis, never an undisclosed truncation. Reviewed candidate identities
3675	follow a stable source fingerprint within a project, separately from the current
3676	Run, under the workflow review contract.
3677	
3678	Cross-unit reference evidence: `docs/coop/design-corrections/integration-host-model.py`
3679	and `check-integration.py`. The model composes actual reference admissions over
3680	synthetic TCB inputs; it does not execute repository code or measure confinement.
3681	
3682	Public details for the shared cap and explicit-root grammar are PROJECT.WORKSPACE_UNIT_LIMIT and PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID. The pure instrument retains native.too-many-units and native.explicit-root-grammar only as internal aliases; the host normalizes them through public-detail-registry.v1.json, and the public schema rejects those aliases. The internal capability table key provider-unavailable/capability-missing emits native.capability-unavailable publicly.
3683	
3684	The four repository-code child-process effect selections in §5 are consistent with the accepted permission-truth-tables.v9 head. The v7→v9 changes concern metadata/recording and the host-under-instruction network recital; the permission table rows supplying the four selections are unchanged. The product still declares these as its own supported-platform design selections, not measured confinement or an extension of preview qualification.
3685	
3686	
3687	A **bounded selection array** that exceeds its published schema bound refuses REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE (request-rejected, exit2), public detail PROJECT.SCOPE_LIMIT and subject `field:count>limit`; it is never truncated. **Seven** fields are bounded this way, across **three record families**, and the subject always names which one overflowed. The **scope descriptor** family contributes three: workspaceRoots has limit1024 (distinct roots after co-located unit deduplication), and pathPrefixes/excludedPathPrefixes each65536; thus1025..4096 valid discovered unit roots produce this typed scope refusal, while more than4096 first-party unit directories produce PROJECT.WORKSPACE_UNIT_LIMIT earlier. The **analysis-spec** array `requestedCapabilities` has limit1024, and it overflows for a reason worth stating: the matrix-fixed default requests one row per (discovered unit, capability whose cell is not NOT-SELECTED), which is11 capabilities per TypeScript unit and10 per Rust unit, so93 TypeScript units fit, at1023 rows - one row under the bound, not exactly at it - and94 do not, at1034. Units94..1024 are therefore ordinary repositories the scope law admits and the default analysis cannot express, and they refuse HERE rather than through a generic schema exception that carries no typed scope projection — no public detail, no class or exit, no `field:count>limit` subject and no per-field remedy — even though its own structured fields do identify the failing path and the bound. The public code is shared across host/native scope admission; callers must narrow explicit selection — for `requestedCapabilities` that means fewer workspace roots for the invocation, or an explicit `analysis.capabilities` selection carrying its own provenance. The **Plan** family contributes the remaining three, and they are reachable by ordinary valid selections that every earlier bound admits: `nativeContextDigests` has limit128 and carries one member per DISTINCT admitted native context, so an inventory-only or otherwise narrow capability selection keeps `requestedCapabilities` far below its own1024 while129 units whose compiler closure, standard library and effective options differ pass the workspace bound and cannot be expressed in the Plan; `importIds` has limit256 while the selecting field `semantic-configuration.evidence.importIds` admits1024, so257 imported evidence records are an admitted configuration and an unrepresentable Plan; and `semanticClosures` has limit128 while `policyPackIds` admits128 packs that need not share closures. Those three are accounted **before plan2 is minted**, on the PROSPECTIVE Plan assembled from an already-admitted request, so a refusal mints no Plan and no Run for the refused step. They are **not** a retained-record check: an externally retained Plan over its bound is a corrupt or malformed retained record and keeps its schema-first refusal and this section's origin-dependent routing, because re-deriving a caller's remedy from already-committed bytes would misreport a corrupt store as an oversized request. Only an ACTUAL array over its bound refuses on cardinality; a missing field, null, boolean, number, string or object is a shape the schema owns and reaches it untouched. When more than one array of an assembled prospective Plan overflows at once the subject is the first in the published `$defs/plan` declaration order — `semanticClosures`, `nativeContextDigests`, `importIds` — so one request always yields one subject and narrowing makes deterministic progress. That order governs the prospective-Plan boundary, among the fields present there. It is not an ordering claim about the whole request: `nativeContextDigests` is also accounted at the earlier producer boundary that computes, admission-validates and deduplicates the native contexts, and an overflow refuses there before any prospective Plan is assembled. Native ScopeRefusal retains detail, D9 and observed bound fields for the host's closed termination projection, and is already field-generic, so all seven fields use one law and one code: the remedy class is identical — narrow the selection explicitly, nothing was truncated — which is why widening it across the further record families adds no public code, while each field keeps its OWN remedy wording because what a caller narrows differs per field.
3688	
3689	The **pre-Plan admission order** is published, because it is what makes the typed refusal reachable. A complete `analysis-spec` - defaulted or explicitly supplied - is admitted in three steps: **bounded selection cardinality first**, then generic schema validation of the whole record, then the closed native capability vocabulary. Cardinality precedes schema validation because a `maxItems` breach is reported generically: the exception restates the entire instance and carries no typed scope projection — no public detail, class, exit, `field:count>limit` subject or per-field remedy — even though its own structured fields do identify the failing path and the bound; an oversized ordinary selection is not a malformed record and is not published as one. The first step is **conditional on the field actually being a JSON array in an object**, and nothing is coerced: a missing field, a null, a boolean, a number, a string or an object proceeds untouched to the schema step and refuses there as the malformed record it is. Without that condition a 1025-character string would be published as 1025 capabilities, which is a misclassification and not a scope limit. Everything a schema is genuinely better at - an unknown property, a wrong type, a missing field, a missing `schemaVersion` - still refuses at the schema step exactly as before, **for every input that reaches that step**. Which inputs those are follows from the condition, not from the bound alone: step 1 refuses **only** an actual JSON array that is over its bound, so a spec whose `requestedCapabilities` is **absent, null, a boolean, a number, a string or an object** proceeds untouched to the schema step and refuses there as the malformed record it is, and so does an array **within** its bound that is malformed in any other way. The ordering is exact and cardinality-first, so an input that is *both* an oversized array and otherwise malformed refuses with the cardinality result - `PROJECT.SCOPE_LIMIT`, subject `field:count>limit` - and its schema fault is reported on a later, narrowed request rather than in the same one. Nothing is lost or misclassified by that: the malformed spec is refused either way, no Plan or Run is minted for the refused step, and the refusal that does fire states a true fact about the instance. **The two routes are not, however, the same public termination, and this paragraph does not flatten them.** The cardinality refusal is origin-independent - `request-rejected` (2), `REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE`, `PROJECT.SCOPE_LIMIT` - because an oversized ordinary selection is not malformed. The schema refusal keeps §10's **origin-dependent** routing: an externally supplied or retained spec is `request-rejected` (2) / `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, while a host-generated internal layer minting its own invalid spec is **`operational-failed` (4)** / `SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE` with `faultCause: host-invariant`. Reordering the two steps therefore never converts a host-invariant fault into a request rejection, and never the reverse. One condition is reordered for one shape, and none is added. This order is the **request** boundary only. Validation of a **retained** `analysis-spec` payload at Run closure is a different question with a different answer - an oversized array there means corruption rather than an oversized request - and nothing here changes it: Run closure schema-validates the retained record before any capability vocabulary admission, so an over-long retained array already refuses there.
3690	
3691	What this refusal is **not**. It is not a truncation: no capability is dropped, no root is dropped, and the matrix-fixed default and every advertised capability promise are unchanged. It is not a host defect: the host computed the default correctly and the *request* simply cannot be expressed within a published bound, so it is `request-rejected`/`REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE` and never `host-invariant`. It is not a licence to shard the invocation, execute extra steps or raise a bound — any of those would be a new product capability and none is selected here. And it is **pre-Plan for the analysis step it refuses**: that step mints no `plan2` and no `run3`. That is a statement about the step, not about attribution - the request and the invocation keep their ordinary operational attribution under the workflow law, and any earlier step of the same invocation that already committed an outcome keeps it. A pure helper `ValidationError` is not a public termination, which is exactly why the typed refusal exists.
3692	
3693	The standalone boundary-crossing key native.explicit-root-crosses-boundary is an internal alias of PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID, the code security emits before native on the operational path. native.boundary-inventory-mismatch is an internal alias of PROJECT.DISCOVERY_INVENTORY_MISMATCH. The latter public condition is emitted by the actual host when its native marker/file inventory disagrees with the security discovery inventory (REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED, exit2), including before native is invoked. Neither internal spelling is a public enum value.
